article_title: Simulated directed-learning in life-education intervention on the meaning of life, positive beliefs, and well-being among nursing students: A Quasi-experimental study.
citation: Tsai Fu-Ju PhD, Hu Yih-Jin PhD, Chen Cheng-Yu PhD, Yeh Gwo-Liang PhD, Tseng Chie-Chien PhD, Chen Si-Chi PhD, Tusconi Massimo. (2019). Simulated directed-learning in life-education intervention on the meaning of life, positive beliefs, and well-being among nursing students: A Quasi-experimental study. Medicine. https://doi.org/10.1097/MD.0000000000016330
title: 56-item questionnaire measuring meaning of life, positive beliefs, and well-being
description: A 56-item questionnaire drawn from the Life Attitude Profile by Ho and the Positive Coping, Spirituality and Well-Being Scale by Lin and Yu, used to measure nursing students' views on meaning of life (1–25 items), positive beliefs (1–11 items), and well-being (1–20 items) on a 5-point Likert scale from "completely disagree" 1 to "completely agree" 5. Content validity index was 0.95 by 7 expert scholars; Cronbach's α was 0.96, 0.95, and 0.96 respectively (n = 45).
requirements: Administered three times at pre-test, post-test, and post-post-test to all participants
constraints: Reliability estimated with a subsample of n = 45 as printed in the article
examples: Used to collect all 110 complete questionnaires from May 1 to June 21, 2018
